detection_signals.note: infrastructure as code, not application code: a file that only exists because somebody declares desired state or a pipeline (persona doc 9.2 'desired-state source of truth', 9.5 tool adapters). Two exclusions are deliberate. '.github/workflows/' is NOT a signal even though it is a CI pipeline definition, because almost every repository on this estate carries one and a signal every repository matches makes this lens win everywhere; the narrower CI files above (GitLab, Jenkins, Azure Pipelines, CircleCI) are only present where somebody is actually maintaining a pipeline. 'docker-compose.yml' is NOT a signal because it is as often a local development convenience as an infrastructure artifact. Estate reach measured 2026-09-04 with git ls-files and find over the working trees: the hub matches on exactly one path, products/brothermode/azure-pipelines.yml; the other two local repositories checked (a token-economy tooling repository and a client analysis workspace) match nothing. No signal here collides with core (core has none) or with data-science (*.ipynb, mlruns/, dvc.yaml, dbt_project.yml, mlflow, dvc, dbt_project), and infer_lens tries packs in sorted lens-name order, so data-science is tried before infrastructure-senior and keeps its own fixture.

challenge_question: Is a replace/destroy operation acceptable in this environment, and what is the maximum blast radius?

question_budget.work_shape: Production infra change (persona doc 4.2, 'Production infra change' 2 to 6). The same table sets no fixed cap for a high-risk irreversible, security or spend change: when a forcing class below fires, max is advisory and the necessary decisions are still asked (4.2, 'no fixed cap; require necessary decisions').

forcing_classes.label: Destroy or replace
forcing_classes.why: the saved plan JSON has a resource_changes entry whose change.actions is ["delete"] or contains both "create" and "delete" (a replace), or the diff removes a resource block from a .tf file, or it edits an attribute the provider marks ForceNew. Persona doc 9.3 INF-01 and 25.2 ('Infrastructure: planned destroy/replace of stateful production resource').

forcing_classes.label: Privilege widening
forcing_classes.why: the diff adds or edits an IAM policy, role, role binding or trust policy (aws_iam_*, google_project_iam_*, azurerm_role_assignment, a Kubernetes Role, ClusterRole, RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding), or a policy document gains "*" in an Action or Resource field, or a service account gains a new binding. Persona doc 9.3 INF-02, 9.4 point 5 ('widen permissions'), 25.1 ('widening production privilege').

forcing_classes.label: Network exposure
forcing_classes.why: a security group, firewall rule or network policy in the diff gains 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, or a Kubernetes Service type changes to LoadBalancer or NodePort, or an Ingress gains a host, or an attribute named publicly_accessible, public_network_access_enabled or public_ip_address is set true. Persona doc 9.3 INF-05, 9.4 point 5 ('expose network paths').

forcing_classes.label: Secret in configuration
forcing_classes.why: the diff assigns a literal value (not a reference to a secret manager, a variable or a sealed reference) to a key whose name contains password, secret, token, api_key, private_key or credential, in a .tf, .tfvars, values.yaml, .env or Kubernetes manifest, or adds a Secret object with stringData written inline. Persona doc 9.2 (secrets), 9.3 INF-07, 9.4 point 5 ('rotate').

forcing_classes.label: Cost change
forcing_classes.why: the diff changes a priced dimension: instance_type, machine_type, node_count, replicas, min_size, max_size, desired_capacity, disk or volume size, a provisioned throughput or capacity unit, or an autoscaling bound. Persona doc 3.2 (money includes cloud spend), 9.3 INF-09 and INF-13, 9.4 point 5 ('spend materially').

forcing_classes.label: Rollback path absent
forcing_classes.why: the unit's receipt carries rollback_path_and_exercised as NO-DATA while plan_summary counts a destroy or a replace above zero, or a stateful resource (a database instance, a persistent volume claim, a StatefulSet, a bucket with a lifecycle rule) is in the diff and backup_restore_status is NO-DATA. Persona doc 9.3 INF-17 and INF-22, 9.6 ('whether actually exercised').

forcing_classes.label: Production mutation
forcing_classes.why: the changed path or the resolved workspace names a production environment (a path segment prod, production or live; a file production.tfvars or values-prod.yaml; a terraform workspace or kube context whose name matches those words) AND the action the unit intends is apply, upgrade, rollout or delete rather than plan, template, diff or dry-run. Persona doc 9.4 point 4 ('production mutation requires an explicit human decision for high-impact actions').

work_classes.label: infrastructure/configuration change
work_classes.why: the pack's home class: desired state, pipelines and platform configuration (persona doc 3.1 item 7).

work_classes.label: release / deployment
work_classes.why: rollout strategy, maintenance window and rollback are this persona's own intake dimensions (9.2), and INF-03 and INF-08 are rollout and pipeline units.

work_classes.label: incident investigation
work_classes.why: INF-14, whose critical failure is destructive remediation, and whose default evidence is a read-only evidence graph first (9.3, 9.4 point 1).

work_classes.label: performance/cost optimization
work_classes.why: INF-09 and INF-13: capacity and cost work whose failure mode is a reliability regression bought with a saving.

work_classes.label: security/privacy hardening
work_classes.why: INF-02, INF-05, INF-07 and INF-19: IAM, network boundary, secret rotation and image vulnerability work.

work_classes.label: dependency/platform migration
work_classes.why: INF-11 (cluster or node upgrade) and INF-19 (base image upgrade), where the risk is workload incompatibility rather than a defect in the change itself.

work_classes.label: defect / incident correction
work_classes.why: INF-15, incident remediation, whose critical failure is a symptom patch that lets the incident recur.

work_classes.label: documentation/runbook change
work_classes.why: INF-12 treats a runbook as an artifact to validate, not prose: an alert with no runbook is a blind incident.

work_classes.label: spike/research with no production mutation
work_classes.why: 9.4 points 1 and 2: discover, read, plan and dry-run freely, which is exactly the class where this pack asks the fewest questions.

risk_classes.how_this_lens_scores_it: high whenever plan_summary counts a destroy or a replace, because a replaced managed resource comes back with a new identity, not the old one.
the production_mutation forcing class is exactly this axis made visible: read and plan are free, apply against a production workspace is not.
scored from stateful resources in the diff (databases, volumes, buckets, StatefulSets) and closed only by backup_restore_status with an actual restore, never by a backup that merely exists (INF-17).
scored from the IAM and network deltas; privilege_widening and network_exposure both force a human rather than adjusting tone.
cloud spend is money here (3.2). Scored from the cost_change forcing class and reported as estimated_cost_delta, with the estimator named.
scored from the affected-environment inventory (INF-18): how many environments or tenants consume the changed module, not how large the diff is.
scored from rolling-deployment and dual-version questions: INF-07 (a rotation both old and new consumers must survive) and INF-11 (workloads that must run on the new node version).
an intake dimension of this persona (9.2, compliance and audit requirement); scored from whether the environment carries a stated audit obligation, and recorded rather than assumed away.
the E16 family plus rollback_path_and_exercised: a written rollback with no run is NO-DATA, and rollback_path_absent fires when a destroy or replace sits beside that NO-DATA.

highest where the provider will not say what it will do without applying (a managed service migration, a DNS cutover): those units carry more NO-DATA lines, stated, rather than a plan presented as certainty.

dangerous_actions: applying, upgrading or rolling out anything into a production account, subscription, project or cluster (9.4 point 4)
destroying, deleting, tainting or replacing any resource, in any environment, when the resource holds state (9.4 point 5, 25.2)
widening any permission: adding an IAM policy or binding, granting a role, editing a trust policy, or relaxing a network policy (9.4 point 5, 25.1)
opening a network path to the public internet, or removing one other systems depend on (9.4 point 5)
creating, rotating, revoking or printing any secret, credential, key or certificate private half (9.4 point 5)
committing anything that increases spend materially, including raising an autoscaling ceiling (9.4 point 5)
running a remediation during an incident before the read-only evidence graph exists (INF-14)
reconciling drift by overwriting a change somebody made deliberately during an incident (INF-16)
disabling, silencing or deleting an alert, dashboard or log pipeline (INF-12)
changing a backup, retention or lifecycle policy in a way that shortens what can be recovered (INF-17, INF-21)

know_how.situation: A Terraform or OpenTofu resource change.
know_how.brother_asks: Which environment does this resolve against, and is a replace or destroy acceptable there?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: a saved plan parsed for add, change, destroy and replace, with the destructive-operation gate run over it; the critical failure is an unexpected destroy or replace.

know_how.brother_asks: What exactly does this principal gain, and who decided it needs it?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: a policy diff plus a least-privilege check; the critical failure is privilege escalation.

know_how.brother_asks: How does this roll out, and what does the rollback look like if the new pods never become ready?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: manifest validation plus a rollout and rollback drill; the critical failure is an outage or a failed rollout.

know_how.brother_asks: What do the rendered manifests actually differ by, once values are applied?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: a rendered manifest diff plus schema checks; the critical failure is a hidden rendered diff nobody read because only the values file was reviewed.

know_how.situation: A networking or security group change.
know_how.brother_asks: What should be able to reach what after this, stated as intent before the rule is read?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the reachability intent written down, then the policy diff checked against it; the critical failure is lost connectivity or new exposure.

know_how.brother_asks: What is the TTL, and how long is the window where both the old and the new value must work?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: staged validation plus a rollback plan that accounts for the TTL; the critical failure is an outage or a failed cutover.

know_how.brother_asks: Can both the old and the new value be valid at once, and for how long?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: redaction proven over logs and output, plus a dual-version compatibility check; the critical failure is a leak or an incompatible rollout.

know_how.brother_asks: Which gate does this change the reachability of, and can any path now skip it?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the pipeline graph plus tests that a protected boundary still refuses; the critical failure is a bypassed gate.

know_how.brother_asks: What load model says this bound is right, and what does the ceiling cost if it is reached?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: a load or capacity model plus the declared limits; the critical failure is a cost blowout or throttling.

know_how.situation: A database or managed service change.
know_how.brother_asks: Does the provider replace rather than modify this, and where is the restore point?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the provider plan plus backup and recovery proof; the critical failure is data or service loss.

know_how.brother_asks: Which workloads use an API or a feature this version removes?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: preflight checks plus representative workload checks on the new version; the critical failure is workload incompatibility.

know_how.brother_asks: Which incident would this alert have caught, and what does the runbook tell the person paged to do?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: alert, query and runbook validation; the critical failure is a blind incident.

know_how.brother_asks: What reliability property is being spent to buy this saving?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the cost delta beside an SLO guard; the critical failure is a reliability regression.

know_how.brother_asks: Nothing that mutates: what does the read-only evidence say first?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: a read-only evidence graph built before any remediation is proposed; the critical failure is destructive remediation.

know_how.brother_asks: What made the bad state possible, and what invariant stops it recurring?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: an incident replay through the new behaviour plus a follow-up invariant; the critical failure is a symptom patch and recurrence.

know_how.brother_asks: Was this drift an accident, or a deliberate emergency change somebody made?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: drift classified per resource, then a human decision on the deliberate ones; the critical failure is overwriting an intentional emergency change.

know_how.brother_asks: When was a restore from this policy last actually performed?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: an actual restore drill, not the existence of backups; the critical failure is a false sense of safety.

know_how.situation: A multi-account or shared module change.
know_how.brother_asks: Every environment that consumes this module: which are they, and which goes first?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: an affected-environment inventory plus a canary in one of them; the critical failure is broad propagation.

know_how.situation: A container or base image upgrade.
know_how.brother_asks: What changed in the image beyond the version string, and does the workload still run on it?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: an SBOM or vulnerability diff plus smoke and integration runs; the critical failure is a runtime or security regression.

know_how.situation: A platform self-service module or feature exposed to developers.
know_how.brother_asks: Which knob does this hand to somebody who will not read the plan?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: a constrained interface plus policy tests over what the module refuses; the critical failure is an unsafe developer knob.

know_how.situation: A queue or storage policy change.
know_how.brother_asks: What becomes unrecoverable after this retention or lifecycle rule takes effect?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the policy diff plus a lifecycle simulation over representative objects; the critical failure is retention loss or data loss.

know_how.brother_asks: What recovery time and data loss does this assume, and has anybody measured them?
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: a recovery-time and data-loss exercise, run; the critical failure is unrecoverable assumptions.

know_how.situation: Brother needs to understand the environment before proposing anything.
know_how.brother_asks: Nothing. Discover and read freely within the granted local or tool scope.
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the orientation record: what was read, each statement marked FACT, INFERENCE, UNKNOWN, HUMAN_DECISION or VAULT_CONTEXT.

know_how.situation: A plan, diff, render or dry-run would answer the question.
know_how.brother_asks: Nothing, when the operation is non-destructive: run it rather than ask.
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the E11 artifact itself (plan JSON, rendered manifests, kubectl diff, GitOps diff), attached to the unit.

know_how.situation: The target is an isolated, local or test environment.
know_how.brother_asks: Nothing beyond the declared autonomy for that environment: write there.
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the run record naming the environment, so the receipt's environment_scope cannot later be read as production.

know_how.situation: The action would mutate production and the impact is high.
know_how.brother_asks: The explicit decision, with the plan summary, the blast radius and the rollback path in front of the human.
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: a recorded human decision; the unit stops at prepared, and production_action_requiring_human_authorization names exactly what was withheld.

know_how.situation: The action destroys, deletes, rotates, spends materially, widens permission or exposes a network path.
know_how.brother_asks: The decision, always: these are forcing conditions and are never inferred approvals, in any environment.
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the fired forcing class recorded with the concrete condition seen in the diff or plan, and the human answer.

know_how.situation: Deciding how many of the above to ask at once.
know_how.brother_asks: Only at the few boundaries where a human actually owns the risk.
know_how.proof_that_closes_it: the question budget honoured (2 to 6 for a production infra change), each question passing the stage 2 value test: the answer could change scope, architecture, risk, route, evidence, rollout or acceptance.

tool_adapters.what_it_gives: the E11 spine: add, change, destroy and replace per resource, machine readable.
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for plan_summary; the unit says the plan was not produced and why, and never infers the counts from the diff.

tool_adapters.what_it_gives: provider-aware lint over the IaC itself (E10).
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for the lint line; other E10 evidence may still close the unit.

tool_adapters.what_it_gives: IaC policy findings: Checkov, tfsec or an equivalent (E10, E14).
tool_adapters.detect: command -v checkov || command -v tfsec || command -v trivy
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for the policy line, stated with the scanner names tried.
NO-DATA for estimated_cost_delta; a provider native estimate may substitute when it is named.

tool_adapters.what_it_gives: rendered manifests and chart lint, which is what INF-04 compares.
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for the rendered diff; a values-file diff is not a substitute and is not offered as one.

tool_adapters.what_it_gives: schema validation of Kubernetes manifests (E10): kubeconform or kubeval.
kubectl diff and read-only status, the cluster's own view of the change (E11, E15).
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for the live diff; the unit stays at the rendered-manifest level.

tool_adapters.what_it_gives: policy as code over plans and manifests (E10).
image vulnerability and SBOM evidence for INF-19 (E14).
tool_adapters.detect: command -v trivy || command -v grype || command -v syft
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for the image line; a version bump alone never closes INF-19.

tool_adapters.what_it_gives: what the cluster's reconciler would actually apply (E11): Argo CD or Flux output.
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for the GitOps diff; in a GitOps estate this absence is itself worth reporting, because the repository diff is not the applied diff.

tool_adapters.detect: command -v aws || command -v gcloud || command -v az
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for environment_scope resolved from the provider; the workspace name alone is stated as an inference, not a fact.

tool_adapters.what_it_gives: E15 evidence: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus or Grafana style queries showing the behaviour is visible.
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for observability evidence; INF-12 cannot be closed without it.

tool_adapters.what_it_gives: incident timelines and logs for INF-14 and INF-15 replay.
tool_adapters.detect: the project's own documented incident CLI or export path, read from its runbook rather than guessed
tool_adapters.when_absent: NO-DATA for incident replay; the unit says the remediation was not replayed against a real case.

fixture.note: must_infer_paths carries no data-science signal (no *.ipynb, mlruns/, dvc.yaml or dbt_project.yml), so sorted lens-name order cannot hand this fixture to data-science; must_not_infer_paths is a plain tree that infers no lens at all, which is what scripts/test_door.py's own test_a_plain_tree_infers_no_lens already asserts.

required_evidence_families_why.E11: Dry-run / plan evidence: the lens exists because a plausible looking diff is not a statement about the account it will run in (persona doc 9.1). A terraform or tofu plan JSON, a helm template render, a kubectl diff, a GitOps diff or a provider dry-run is the only artifact that names add, change, destroy and replace before anything mutates, and it is the default evidence of INF-01, INF-04, INF-05, INF-08, INF-10, INF-16 and INF-21. Without it every other family below is reasoning about a change nobody has seen resolved.
required_evidence_families_why.E10: Static structural checks: IaC policy is the cheapest independent oracle this lens has: tflint, Checkov or tfsec, kubeconform schema validation, OPA or Conftest. It is what turns 'the plan looks fine' into 'no rule the team wrote was broken', and it catches the INF-02 and INF-20 failures (privilege escalation, an unsafe self-service knob) that a plan renders without judging.
required_evidence_families_why.E14: Security / privacy tests: the persona's intake dimensions name IAM and permissions, network boundary and secrets (9.2), and three of its forcing conditions are privilege widening, network exposure and secret handling (9.4 point 5). A least-privilege check on the IAM diff, a reachability check on the network diff and a redaction check on rotated material are what make those receipt lines real rather than asserted (INF-02, INF-05, INF-07, INF-19).
required_evidence_families_why.E16: Rollback / restore proof: 9.6 asks for the rollback command AND whether it was actually exercised, and INF-17's critical failure is a backup policy that gives a false sense of safety, closed only by an actual restore drill. A documented rollback path with no run behind it is NO-DATA in this pack, never a pass, and the rollback_path_absent forcing class fires on it.
required_evidence_families_why.E13: Performance / resource tests: cloud spend is money under the doc's own risk axis (3.2, 'money: payments, billing, cloud spend'), and 9.6 asks for an estimated cost delta. INF-09 (autoscaling and capacity) and INF-13 (cost optimization) both fail as cost blowouts or as reliability regressions bought with a saving, so the capacity or cost model is evidence, not a footnote.
required_evidence_families_why.E15: Observability evidence: INF-12's critical failure is a blind incident, and 9.2 lists observability as an intake dimension. A change that cannot be seen succeeding or failing in production has not been proven safe to roll out, whatever the plan said; alert, query and runbook validation is what closes it.

environment_scope.meaning: which account, subscription, project, cluster or workspace this unit actually touched, named exactly as the provider names it, not as prose.
environment_scope.filled_by: command: terraform workspace show, or kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.contexts[0].context.cluster}', or the cloud CLI's own account read (aws sts get-caller-identity, gcloud config get-value project, az account show); NO-DATA when no environment was resolved.

plan_summary.meaning: the four counts a human reads first: add, change, destroy, replace. Replace is counted separately from destroy because a replace of a stateful resource is the failure INF-01 exists for.
plan_summary.filled_by: file: the saved plan JSON (terraform show -json <planfile>), counted from resource_changes[].change.actions; NO-DATA when no plan was produced.

iam_security_delta.meaning: every permission, role, policy, binding or trust relationship this unit widens, narrows or creates, in plain words plus the resource ids.
iam_security_delta.filled_by: file: the policy diff (the plan JSON's iam and role resource_changes, or the rendered manifest's ClusterRole and RoleBinding objects) plus the least-privilege check output; NO-DATA when the change touches no permission surface.

network_delta.meaning: what becomes reachable from where that was not reachable before, and what stops being reachable: security group rules, firewall rules, ingress hosts, service types, peering, DNS records.
network_delta.filled_by: file: the plan JSON or rendered manifest diff filtered to network resources, beside the stated reachability intent; NO-DATA when no network boundary moved.

estimated_cost_delta.meaning: the expected monthly spend difference, with the estimator named and its assumptions stated, because an estimate whose assumptions are hidden is not evidence.
estimated_cost_delta.filled_by: command: infracost diff, or the provider native estimate; NO-DATA when no estimator is installed or the change has no priced resource (the tool_adapters entry says how absence is reported).

blast_radius.meaning: how far a failure of this unit reaches: which environments, which services, how many tenants or users, and whether the effect is contained to one account or propagates across modules.
blast_radius.filled_by: file: the affected-environment inventory (INF-18) listing every environment or module instance that consumes the changed module, plus the plan for each; NO-DATA when the inventory was not built.

slo_availability_risk.meaning: which service level objective or availability commitment this unit could move, and in which direction, stated before the rollout rather than measured after the incident.
slo_availability_risk.filled_by: file: the named SLO or error budget document plus the guard the rollout runs against it; NO-DATA when the service carries no declared SLO.

canary_staging_result.meaning: what happened when this change ran somewhere that is not production first, including the environment name and the observation window.
canary_staging_result.filled_by: command: the rollout or apply run in the non-production environment, with its exit code and output location; NO-DATA when no staging or canary environment exists for this resource, which is itself a finding.

rollback_path_and_exercised.meaning: the exact command or procedure that puts the system back, and the separate fact of whether anybody ran it. Two answers, never one.
rollback_path_and_exercised.filled_by: command: the rollback command itself (helm rollback, kubectl rollout undo, terraform apply of the prior state, the DNS TTL cutover reversal), plus its run record when exercised; NO-DATA for the exercised half when the path is only written down.

backup_restore_status.meaning: for any stateful resource touched: when the last backup was taken, and when a restore from it was last proven to work.
backup_restore_status.filled_by: command: the provider's backup listing plus the restore drill run (INF-17, INF-22); NO-DATA when the unit touches no stateful resource.

production_action_requiring_human_author.meaning: the specific action, if any, that this unit prepared but did not take because a human owns it, named so the human can authorize exactly that and nothing wider.
production_action_requiring_human_author.filled_by: file: the forcing-class record naming the fired class, the condition seen, and the decision asked; NO-DATA when no forcing class fired and nothing was withheld.
